findings.what: "Textbooks add that the line through (2, 4) can also be written y − 4 = 0.5(x − 2)" credits textbooks with no citation. The brief cites SQA National 5 for this form (notes 2.4, 4.4), so either cite that quote or drop "Textbooks add" and just show the bracket form; the expansion itself is correct (y − 4 = 0.5x − 1, so y = 0.5x + 3).

findings.where: step 8 (Mind the brackets), Why? note and working
findings.what: This is the only screen that puts the second point (1, 7) in for c, and nothing says why. Add a few words such as "(1, 7) has no minus signs, so it is the easier one to put in", which also teaches that either point works.

Points are to be read "where it crosses grid lines exactly" without saying why (any other point is only an estimate). The advice to use the axis numbers "because the two axes often have different scales" is never shown, because every grid in the lesson is squared at the same scale.

"Set it to a marked slope with your level" does not match how an ordinary spirit level works: it shows level and plumb, not an arbitrary slope. "Line it up with a slope marked on the wall" or "an angle finder" would ring true for an electrician.

While the line is still swinging, the working panel under the grid is a tall empty bordered box (its rows are reserved but invisible) for about 2.5 s. It does stop the page jumping, but it reads as dead space; a faint "y = ?" row, like the puzzles have, would fill it.
